Restoring Artifacts

Source: vignettes/restore-artifacts.Rmd
restore-artifacts.Rmd

Use projr_get_github() or projr_get_local() to copy files for a completed build into a folder of your choice. To rerun an analysis, use projr_restore() in its checkout, then run projr_build_dev().

Get files from a completed build

These examples work outside a projr project. The first downloads reports from a GitHub Release. The second copies results from an analysis on disk and works without Git or a network connection.

library(projr)

reports <- projr_get_github(repo = "owner/study@analysis",
                            label = "docs", version = "1.2.3", out = "received")
list.files(reports[["docs"]])

results <- projr_get_local(path = "../study", label = "output", out = "received")
list.files(results[["output"]])

In the GitHub example, analysis is the branch containing the study code and 1.2.3 is the build you want. Omit the branch to use the repository’s default branch. When you know the release address, use its repository and tag directly. For example, this reads from the release named reports in a separate repository.

projr_get_github(repo = "owner/study-results", tag = "reports",
                 label = "docs", version = "1.2.3", out = "received")

Omit version to select the most recent completed build recorded at the source. Supply one label or a vector of labels, such as c("raw-data", "docs"). With label = NULL, projr looks up the labels recorded for that build in the source manifest. A historical copy requires files matching the recorded paths and hashes.

Each label gets its own subfolder, such as received/docs/. A relative out starts in your working directory. Its default is ".". Downloads to the same folder use a small .projr-get.lock file to take turns. The returned character vector gives the absolute path of each subfolder, named by label. projr stages and verifies the files before installing them. It keeps matching files and reports conflicting local changes or extra files. Set overwrite = TRUE when you want projr to replace the contents of the requested subfolders.

Inside a project, you can read a named archive from its remotes configuration. For example, the following reads the local archive called shared in the configuration reference.

projr_get_local(remote = "shared", label = "output-figures", out = "received")

Use either remote or the direct address (path for local projects, repo for GitHub). A registered GitHub archive can likewise be selected with projr_get_github(remote = "reports", ...). If the type is stored in a variable, projr_get(type, ...) accepts "local" and "github" and forwards the remaining arguments to the corresponding function.

Rebuild a checked-out version

After checking out a production build or its follow-up development commit, run projr_restore() in the clone. For a project published with projr_build_patch(archive_github = TRUE), the release named archive already contains the required inputs. Each raw directory is restored to its configured path. You can then render the checked-out scripts with projr_build_dev().

projr_restore()
projr_build_dev()

projr first tries files archived for the checked-out version, then earlier uploads with the same directory contents. It recovers missing manifest data from the release and verifies the complete file list and MD5 hashes before installing any downloads. If the checkout lacks both DESCRIPTION and VERSION, projr can recover the version from its .projr/BUILDLOG.md. You can also supply version = "1.2.3".

A partially populated input directory is filled when its existing files match. To replace local edits or remove extra files, supply clear = TRUE. For a templated release, pass its recorded concrete tag with destination.

When builds share the same inputs

For example, the Tutu analysis used the same four raw input files in v0.2.0 and v0.6.1. Its checkout records v0.2.0 as the first build with that file list. Its GitHub archive first recorded the list at v0.6.1. You can see both records in the checkout’s version history and the release’s manifest.zip.

In a checkout containing those builds, this comparison returns zero changed files.

projr_manifest_changes("v0.2.0", "v0.6.1", label = "raw-data")

The comparison reads the checkout’s history. When you restore the earlier build, projr 0.7.0 and later can use a later upload if the exact and earlier copies are unavailable. The release must record the same snapshot, and every downloaded filename and hash must match.

Check whether a build reproduces

Run projr_reproduce() to check whether an analysis still produces the exact files it recorded. It clones the project, restores its raw inputs and runs the production scripts from empty output folders. The configured inputs, outputs and cache must be inside the clone. Archives can live elsewhere. Choose a project whose scripts and hooks you trust.

result <- projr_reproduce("owner/study", branch = "analysis", path = "study-check")
result$exact
result$directories
subset(result$files, status != "identical")
Arguments Code and expected files
Neither version nor commit The latest completed build on the selected branch.
version = "1.2.3" The code, inputs and expected outputs for that build.
commit alone The last completed build at or before the commit, using that build’s code.
Both The specified commit’s code with the named version’s inputs and expected outputs.

A lockfile supplies the package versions for the run. With only a DESCRIPTION, pak installs the dependencies and their versions are unpinned. Inspect result$dependencies$packages to see which versions were available. The overall result is true only when every expected directory has a recorded baseline and the relative filenames and bytes all match. Inspect result$files to see which files changed, went missing or appeared. For example, a PDF can have matching text and still differ in its metadata. The results stay in the checkout you selected with path.

projr_restore_repo()

Clones a GitHub repository and restores artifacts in one step.

projr_restore_repo(
  repo,          # "owner/repo" or "repo"
  path = NULL,   # clone destination (default: subdirectory named after repo)
  label = NULL,  # which artifacts (default: all raw-* labels)
  pos = NULL,    # "source", "dest", or both (default: both)
  type = NULL,   # "github" or "local" (default: first available)
  title = NULL,  # remote title from _projr.yml
  destination = NULL  # original concrete release tag or local path
)
# Clone into a subdirectory
projr_restore_repo("owner/repo")

# Clone to a specific path
projr_restore_repo("owner/repo", path = "~/projects/my-analysis")

The function reads _projr.yml in the cloned repo to locate configured remotes, then downloads all raw-* artifacts by default. Cache is not included unless requested explicitly. Returns TRUE on success.

projr_restore_repo_wd()

A convenience wrapper that clones directly into the current working directory.

projr_restore_repo_wd(
  repo,
  label = NULL,
  pos = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  destination = NULL
)
setwd("~/projects/my-analysis")
projr_restore_repo_wd("owner/repo")

This writes files into your current directory, so make sure you are in the right place before calling it.

projr_content_update()

Restores artifacts in an existing local project (no cloning). The project must have a build history in .projr/manifests/ or a legacy root manifest.csv.

projr_content_update(
  label = NULL,  # which artifacts (default: all raw-* labels)
  pos = NULL,    # "source", "dest", or both
  type = NULL,   # "github" or "local"
  title = NULL,  # remote title from _projr.yml
  clear = FALSE,
  destination = NULL
)
# Restore everything raw
projr_content_update()

# Restore raw data and cache
projr_content_update(label = c("raw-data", "cache"))

# Restore from a specific remote
projr_content_update(type = "local", title = "network-backup")

If the project has no manifest, the project needs at least one successful projr_build_*() run first.

Parameters

  • label – character vector of directory labels to restore. NULL (default) restores all raw-* labels. Valid labels include raw-data, cache, output, and docs. Prefer regenerating output/docs with projr_build_dev() rather than restoring them.

  • type – remote type: "github" or "local". NULL (default) uses the first available remote in _projr.yml order.

  • title – selects a specific remote configuration when multiple exist for the same type. NULL (default) uses the first available.

  • pos – "source" for source directories, "dest" for build destinations, or both (the default). Usually the default is fine.

  • repo (restore_repo functions only) – GitHub repository in "owner/repo" or "repo" format.

  • path (projr_restore_repo only) – where to clone. NULL creates a subdirectory; "." clones into the current directory.

Authentication

projr 0.7.0 installs httr for GitHub downloads. If you restore an older renv project pinned to projr 0.6.1 and see a missing-httr error, run renv::install("httr") in that project, then retry the download.

For private GitHub artifacts, use a credential with access to the project. Run projr_instr_auth_github() for instructions. A local destination needs read access to the folder.

Selecting an earlier destination

When a build expands @branch or @uuid in a destination, copy the concrete tag or path from its .projr/BUILDLOG.md. Select the configuration by its title and supply the earlier location as destination.

projr_content_update(
  label = "output", pos = "dest", type = "github",
  title = "study-@branch", destination = "study-site-a"
)

Within that destination, restore selects its latest available version for the label. By default, it retains extra local files. Use clear = TRUE if you want the local label to match the restored payload, including an explicitly recorded empty directory.

Configuring remotes

To publish files for other readers, define a named archive under remotes and select its labels under build, as shown in the configuration reference. A registered archive remains readable when it is absent from the current build settings.

For an existing configuration that keeps the address and publishing settings together under build, use projr_yml_dest_add_github() or projr_yml_dest_add_local() to configure destinations in _projr.yml:

# Archive raw data to GitHub releases
projr_yml_dest_add_github(
  title = "raw-data-@version",
  content = "raw-data",
  send_cue = "if-change"
)

# Archive to a local directory
projr_yml_dest_add_local(
  title = "backup",
  content = "raw-data",
  path = "/mnt/shared/project-data"
)

Add restoration instructions to your project README so collaborators know what to run:

## Setup

1. Restore project: `projr::projr_restore_repo("owner/repo")`
2. Install dependencies: `renv::restore()`
3. Build project: `projr::projr_build_dev()`

Examples

New collaborator setup 

# Clone and restore artifacts
projr_restore_repo("satvilab/my-study")

# Enter project, install dependencies, build
setwd("my-study")
renv::restore()
projr_build_dev()

Selective restoration in an existing project 

# Restore only raw data (skip cache, output, etc.)
projr_content_update(label = "raw-data")

# Regenerate everything else
projr_build_dev()

Falling back between remotes 

# Try GitHub first, fall back to local
result <- tryCatch(
  projr_content_update(type = "github"),
  error = function(e) FALSE
)

if (!result) {
  projr_content_update(type = "local")
}

Notes

  • projr_content_update() selects the latest available version in the chosen destination. Use projr_restore() for the verified inputs of a specific build.

  • The default content-update search looks for a directory’s configured source before checking a build destination that contains that label.

  • projr_content_update() catches errors per label. projr_restore() verifies all downloaded directories before installing them.

  • For debug output, set Sys.setenv(PROJR_OUTPUT_LEVEL = "debug") before restoring.
